paper.title_en: Poster: Everything Good Comes in 3s: How a Qutrit Port Enables Quantum Advantage
paper.abstract_en: Advancements in pushing quantum logic onto many diversified devices have created additional interconnectivity issues and complicated interoperability prospects. However, with advancements in quantum logical sensing and hybridized continuous-discrete quantum logical circuit algorithms on quantum information processing units (QPUs), these approaches can be further used to characterize and design quantum logical interconnects that hold some prospects of quantum physical modality agnosis. With such theoretical improvements for interconnect information, quantum logical interconnects can be used for designing quantum ports for devices, such as for connecting quantum sensors to QPUs as well as architectural approaches for distributed quantum sensing networks, hybrid continuous-discrete QPU busses, and an elusive "quantum USB".We identify that using SU(3) qutrits allows us to capture several of these above characteristics that can internally embed SU(2) qubits coupled to continuous bosons for physical interconnectivity and communications networking along with being coupled to primitive model U(1) noisy p-bits as a conjoint U(2) Hamiltonian evolving system to recapitulate some probabilistically typical bit flip errors of qubit modalities. In this way, we anticipate that future work using SU(3) qutrits when interconnected in a network can also help support isolation from external noises but also segregationally internalize error correction methods such that external SU(3) qutrit logical gate operations can be further programmed to suppress and manipulate U(1) noisy p-bit random operations to error correct SU(2) qubits that are photonically coupled.
